topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Context
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the topic of the lecture and frames the difficulty and importance of studying the complement system.

topics.label: Fundamentals, Nomenclature, and the Central Role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the core architecture, historical naming conventions, and the central biochemical role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three upstream recognition pathways that drive C3 convertase formation and surface deposition.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream processes through which activated complement eradicates pathogens via opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: It details the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that protect host tissues from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical Manifestations of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the distinct clinical presentations and disease outcomes resulting from deficiencies in individual complement pathway components.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion Strategies and Practical Applications
topics.groupedBecause: It explores how microorganisms evade complement attack, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary model, and how these mechanisms are applied in biotechnology.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It provides closing framing for the session and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
